anomaly_alerts.title: How these numbers are counted
anomaly_alerts.description: Read as manufacturing data (failures, assets). Ratios pool their parts (OEE and availability over planned production time, summed over shifts and machines before dividing), so a line's figure pools its machines' time; MTBF is run time per failure and assumes a constant failure rate; MTTR runs from actual start to actual finish of finished repairs. Readings are averaged, not time-weighted. The data covers 3 months, so month-over-month changes may be seasonal; there is no same month last year to compare with. A reading is a level: it is averaged over the period (each reading counts once; not time-weighted), never summed.

executive_view.headline: This manufacturing sensor dataset covers 6,624 readings across 12 assets from Aug 2026 to Oct 2026, tracking temperature, vibration, and failures.

paragraphs.text: The dataset is clean and complete, with temperature and vibration readings largely stable across sensors and the three-month period.
Sensor S07 stands out with a noticeably higher average temperature than all other sensors, which warrants attention.

findings.text: Sensor S07 averages 72.30°C, while all other sensors cluster between 69.88°C and 70.10°C — S07 sits meaningfully above the rest.
There were 155 failures recorded across the dataset; the failure column has a median of 0 and a mean of 0.0234, confirming failures are rare events.
Vibration readings range from 0.102 to 10.73, with a mean of 2.38 and a median of 2.10, suggesting most readings are low but some outliers reach far outside the usual range.
Temperature rose 3.5% month-over-month from Sep 2026 to Oct 2026; because only three months of data are available, it is not possible to tell whether this is seasonal.
Average temperature: S07 (72.30) is higher than S12 (69.88).
Vibration and failure move together in the data: an association, not proof that one causes the other; with medium confidence (weak association (|r| = 0.20)), even that may not hold.
